name: Holmes: The Fourth Case · English
description: You are Holmes. Someone is turning the scenes of a serial novel into real crimes — find out who, and stop the fourth before it happens today.

intro.hook: You are Sherlock Holmes. Someone is staging a serial novel’s illustrations as real crimes, one by one — stop the fourth picture before noon.
loop: Visit the print shop, the editor’s office and the witnesses on the London map
Search the scenes, roll for clues and question everyone
With enough clues, unmask who turned a novel into a crime

characters.line: Your old friend, who promised to protect Edith
The novelist who corrected chapter four’s address herself; frightened, but set on telling it plainly
The print shop’s typesetter, who reads dates and times straight from the duty log

intro.unfinished: Work in progress: the new ending art is still being tested.

author: Worldlines Canvas / AIRP

characters.description: A physician and Holmes's friend, who has promised to protect Edith. This morning he confirmed that the third incident matched its illustration, and he wants today's fourth stopped. He brings a doctor's eye and a human conscience, and leaves the final deduction to Holmes.
characters.name: Watson

characters.description: Watson's patient, a novelist. She is the one who changed the address in chapter four. Frightened, but determined to explain in her own words.
characters.name: Edith Vale

characters.description: The print shop's typesetter: ink-blackened fingers and a duty log. Plain-spoken, he reads out dates and times exactly as recorded.
characters.name: Tom Hale

characters.description: An editor who handles manuscripts and proofs, precise about dates and times and anxious for the paper's reputation.
characters.name: Editor Blackburn

characters.description: An illustrator for serialized novels, with ultramarine-stained cuffs and a right wrist he keeps guarding. Touchy about criticism of his work.
characters.name: Arthur Wayne

endings.title: The One Not in the Fourth Picture
What Was Kept, What Was Missed

mysteries.question: Who turned Edith’s novel into real events, one by one?
mysteries.hint: Whose hands touched those pictures first?

options.label: Edith herself — to make the novel famous
Arthur Wayne, the illustrator
options.epilogue: Wayne’s name was struck from the serial’s credit line. At the print shop they remember him only by the streak of ultramarine that never washed out of his cuff.

options.label: Wayne — the paper was dropping his illustrations, and he wanted all London to see his pictures first
options.title: The Returned Proofs
options.epilogue: The stack of returned proofs went into a Scotland Yard evidence bag. Reading his own red-pencil notes on them, Editor Blackburn changed his mind for the first time: from now on the serial prints its illustrations, with the artist’s name.

options.label: Editor Blackburn — to sell more papers

mysteries.question: What were the three incidents staged after?
mysteries.hint: Compare the time on the delivery slip with the time of the incident.

options.label: The novel’s text — the culprit is an obsessed reader
The illustrations — each picture reached the print shop before its incident
options.epilogue: The Morning Post ran a notice: serial illustrations are now delivered on the day of printing. Tom the typesetter says it is the slowest rule change he has ever seen, and the most sensible.

options.label: Wayne’s own pictures — the scenes held things the novel never mentions
options.title: There Is No Hat in the Novel
options.epilogue: Edith laid the manuscripts of the three incidents beside the illustrations and circled in red what the pictures added: the hat, the chair. At last, she said, she could be sure it was not her story.

mysteries.question: Why did Edith change the fourth chapter’s address to a street that doesn’t exist?
mysteries.hint: Look for that street on the map.

options.label: To lure the culprit to that street and lie in wait
To see who read the new address — and gave himself away when he couldn’t find the street
options.epilogue: Edith kept the street that doesn’t exist in the final fourth chapter. Readers take it for a novelist’s fancy; only Watson knows it was the bolt she put on her own door.

options.label: It was just a slip of the pen

mysteries.question: How did the manuscript with the changed address reach the culprit?
mysteries.hint: Whose name is signed on the editor’s circulation log?

options.label: Tom peeked at it while setting type
Editor Blackburn passed it to Wayne at 8:15, as usual
options.epilogue: Blackburn changed the rules of his office: corrections now pass only between author and editor, and anyone who wants to see one reads it at his desk.

options.label: Wayne went asking for the street the moment he had it — the fake address hooked him that very morning
options.title: The Man Who Asked the Way
options.epilogue: The old map-seller on the corner knew the face in the photograph: “That’s him. Blue on his cuff, asked three times where that street was.” Edith’s test had worked sooner than anyone thought.

options.label: Edith handed it to him herself

epilogues.all: All four secrets are out. When Baker Street talks about that noon, someone always mentions the hat that was never in the novel — and Edith, who finished her fourth chapter with an address of her own.
epilogues.most: You saw most of it. The rest only Wayne knows; but at least no one treats Edith’s novel as a script for crime anymore.
epilogues.few: Noon has passed, but too much behind the three incidents is still unsaid. Perhaps when the next installment runs, you will go and look at the print shop again.

triggers.label: Enough evidence: Wayne turns up
triggers.fallback: Someone calls to you from the corner. Arthur Wayne stands in the fog with a red envelope: “Mr. Holmes — I was just on my way to Miss Vale.”

triggers.label: Every place searched, too little found: Wayne turns up anyway
triggers.fallback: Someone calls to you from the corner. Arthur Wayne stands in the fog with a red envelope: “Mr. Holmes — I was just on my way to Miss Vale.”
